versions.rationale: One patch for an additive, supported protocol-compatibility decision rule. No unrelated metadata change or further increments.

reviewCriteria: Preserve ambassador's design/review scope and identify effective client, proxy and upstream contracts rather than pattern labels.
Check initial handshake direction and availability of routing metadata before selecting a deferred connection mechanism.
Preserve address/authority/SNI/verified identity, attempt and deadline ownership, shard ownership, selection unit, live-stream cutover and shadow isolation.
Require actual version/configuration and an observation point that proves protocol progress; distinguish local fixture, source review and deployed behavior.

findings.before: Protocol compatibility was required, but no instruction identified the circular wait when upstream connection is gated on client bytes while the client waits for the server's greeting.
findings.evidence: Envoy TCP proxy documentation excludes waiting-for-downstream-data mode for server-first protocols. MySQL 8.0.46 source documentation places server greeting before client response and optional TLS negotiation. Existing package search found no first-speaker/handshake-order decision.
findings.consequence: A connected local TCP listener can still leave the operation unable to start; increasing a timeout or retrying the same dependency cycle does not repair it.
findings.correction: Add a short route from local-contract workflow to a focused conditional subsection. Inspect actual first speaker and metadata availability; preserve a route able to connect before greeting or require a supported protocol-aware contract. Retain deferred connection as a valid client-first alternative.
findings.validation: Synthetic loopback probe exercised adverse server-first/deferred path plus server-first/immediate and client-first/deferred controls. No real proxy/DB/TLS execution.

changes: Route TCP/protocol-detection decisions to first-message and connection-establishment checks.
Explain server-first circular wait, MySQL greeting-before-TLS ordering, valid immediate/handshake-aware alternatives, and the legitimate client-first deferred case.
Require actual handshake completion and upstream-connect/byte observations; preserve TLS/authentication and bounded inspection assumptions.
Add primary source references and one patch bump.
preserved: Review/design role; no blanket implementation or infrastructure rollout workflow.
Client-library and existing-mesh alternatives, independent rollout conditions and measured proxy cost.
Separate connection address, HTTP authority, TLS SNI and verified identity; no bypass of mandatory security.
Retry owner, total attempts, replayability, server deduplication, shrinking deadline and unknown effects.
Authoritative shard ownership despite host ejection/failover; mixed-map migration constraints.
Connection/request/stream selection unit; accepted config versus new routing and retirement of old sessions.
Shadow side-effect isolation, resource bounds, measurement denominators and fleet config visibility.
Java compatibility inspection without imposed baseline or new Java examples.
All existing ten shipped teaching cases and their exposure/evaluation limitations.

sources.version: Moving Envoy 1.41.0-dev documentation, accessed 2026-10-16 (page revision changed from bc3dc7 to cb9848 during browsing)
sources.supports: Delayed upstream establishment based on downstream data is unsuitable for server-first protocols; connection trigger and inspection timing are real choices. No configuration flag is prescribed for an unspecified deployed version.
Initial server greeting precedes client handshake response, including optional SSLRequest and TLS exchange.
Router selects cluster per HTTP request; route acquisition is stable within a particular request.
Filter-dependent graceful draining and existing stream lifetime; configuration acceptance alone is not session migration proof.
auto_sni and auto_san_validation are distinct controls, potentially using downstream header-derived inputs.

caseSeparation: Task inputs and criteria are physically separate files. This is procedural separation, not an enforced sandbox. Coordinator must provide actor task files only and withhold criteria and previous probe results. These are development cases derived from the reviewed mechanism, not unseen holdouts.
limitations: Synthetic HELLO/PING/PONG byte protocol over loopback demonstrates the circular dependency and valid alternative only; it does not implement Envoy, MySQL, JDBC, TLS or production authentication.
No real proxy configuration validation, application integration, Kubernetes lifecycle, resource-exhaustion, latency benchmark or production fault test was run.
Inspection timeout values are bounded test guards, not supported production timeout recommendations or hard scheduling guarantees.
Existing security controls were preserved; no TLS verifier or authorization implementation was changed or exercised by the probe.
Moving Envoy documentation is not proof of field support or semantics in an unspecified deployed proxy. MySQL source page is version 8.0.46, not an executed server/client combination.
All material claims of improved decision quality remain expected benefits; only structural and technical checks were executed.
Existing shipped teaching cases remain answer-exposed regression material and were not reclassified as holdouts.
Global verification remains coordinator work after every writer stops.
